acceptanceCriteria: finalize-recovery accepts a complete direct_merge_no_pr receipt when the canonical predecessor is absent and records it through the same strict repository/Git validation as finalize

Historical direct-merge compatibility may use an explicitly historical resource context only under repository, Contract base, real merge commit, parent, and primary-worktree bindings; arbitrary context mismatches remain rejected
finalize-recovery-plan emits all deterministically known receipt identity fields and enumerates human-owned fields without inventing PR, branch, authority, or decision facts
resource identity mismatch diagnostics identify the mismatching binding category and preserve fail-closed behavior
Regression tests cover missing predecessor, valid direct merge apply, foreign repository/work item/Contract context, forged parents, malformed input, symlink, and immutable predecessor bytes
Current-runtime receipts and shared-worktree recovery semantics remain unchanged and existing focused tests pass
English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese command documentation describe the apply boundary and historical_low assurance without claiming provider assurance
No object repository or global configuration files are modified
goal: Provide an auditable, repository-bound apply path for a historical direct merge when no canonical finalization receipt exists, with precise identity diagnostics and regression coverage.
intent: Make historical finalize recovery directly usable for a real legacy direct merge without a pull request, and make resource identity mismatches diagnosable, while preserving immutable predecessor records and current-runtime fail-closed checks.
outOfScope: source Python/Shell/Make implementation and V1 wire compatibility
weakening current Runtime identity checks for active Work Items
release publication and unrelated architecture/performance changes
